subject: Renewal readiness: usage sprint, capacity uplift & SLA ask
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Schulz <markus@orbital.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal readiness: usage sprint, capacity uplift & SLA ask

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. As OrbitalAI approaches the Dec 1 renewal, I wanted to surface the usage sprint we observed in October and outline a practical path to keep your production SLAs stable while preserving unit economics.

Key points from our side:
- October usage: ~54M tokens (up ~42% MoM) — see attached usage-report-Oct-2026.csv for the daily cadence.
- Latency: p95 token latency drifted from 190ms -> 245ms during peak windows (attached latency-dashboard-Oct-2026.png).
- Root cause: bursty batch sizes + longer context generation for the new summarization pipeline.

What we recommend for renewal and the next 90 days:
1) Short-term capacity bridge: +10% committed TPU for Q1 to absorb peaks while we tune batching and prefix caching (this is a temporary uplift, refundable if adoption normalizes).
2) Canary SLA: add a 99.9% p95 latency objective for the top-3 routes with automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant during sustained contention.
3) Cost mitigation: apply adaptive batching and a KV prefix cache to reduce per-token cost by ~6-9% based on the October trace.

Attached: usage-report-Oct-2026.csv, latency-dashboard-Oct-2026.png, and a mutual-action-plan-draft.docx with proposed milestones for rollout.

Can we lock a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the MAP and procurement asks? If procurement needs a high-level econ summary for approvals, I can put together a 1-pager.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123]

[Attachment: latency-dashboard-Oct-2026.png (png, 420KB)]

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal readiness: usage sprint, capacity uplift & SLA ask

Jonas —

Appreciate the thorough breakdown and the attachments. A couple quick items from our side:

- Procurement will need a line-item cost delta for the +10% commit option and an estimate for burst credits if we keep on the current trajectory.
- We run finance approvals on the 18th; any pricing detail you can share ahead of that will make the process smoother.
- For SLAs: acceptable in principle, but engineering wants explicit rollback triggers and a short list of the model variants for automatic fallback.

Can you include a one-page econ summary and the proposed fallback model names in the MAP?

Also forwarding to procurement: procurement@orbital.ai for visibility.

—Markus
Markus Schulz
Head of Product 
OrbitalAI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal readiness: usage sprint, capacity uplift & SLA ask

Markus —

Thanks for the quick reply. Quick internal alignment and a concrete ask to unblock procurement:

1) Pricing delta: +10% committed capacity increases monthly committed spend by ~$12,400 (net after estimated caching savings). I'll attach a one-pager econ summary to this thread by EOD.
2) Burst credits: we can offer a 200k-token monthly burst credit for Q1 as a limited bridge to absorb unexpected peaks.
3) SLA rollback triggers: propose automated rollback if p95 latency exceeds 350ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows; fallback models would be rwd-azimuth-1-small and rwd-azimuth-1-medium (both validated for functional parity on your summarization route).

Next steps (internal): Kimberley, can you draft the econ 1-pager and add the model variant names to the MAP? Laura, please prepare a short note for sales ops on contract amendment language for a temporary 10% uplift and burst credits.

Markus — we propose a 30-minute walkthrough at 3:00pm PT today if that works for you. If procurement needs formal DocuSign-ready term language, we can provide an addendum template for review.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: econ-summary-onepager.pdf (pdf, 9KB) — to follow]

- SLA: add 99.9% p95 objective for top-3 routes with automated fallback to rwd-azimuth-1-small / -medium and the rollback trigger Ben suggested.
- Deliverables for procurement: econ-summary-onepager.pdf, MAP with fallback models, and contract addendum template (DocuSign link to follow).

I've scheduled the 3:00pm PT walkthrough and attached the one-pager and MAP in this thread. If procurement wants a formal spreadsheet with month-by-month delta, Laura will send that within 24 hours.
